title: Star Wars: The Ninth Jedi Director Discusses Lucasfilm Rules
excerpt:
Kenji Kamiyama says creative restrictions increased as a short story became a series.
The director remains positive about the collaboration despite disagreements.
body_md:
Director Kenji Kamiyama has described the creative challenges of expanding Star Wars: Visions' The Ninth Jedi into a full anime series. He said the original shorts offered considerable freedom, but additional franchise rules emerged as the project developed into a longer production.

Kamiyama recalled friction with Lucasfilm over those restrictions, while also emphasizing that working with the people behind Star Wars was personally meaningful. His comments present a more nuanced picture than a simple creative feud: he acknowledged the difficulties and expressed satisfaction with the experience.

The eight-episode limited series is available on Disney+. Its creative team has discussed the possibility of continuing the story, but interest in another season should not be confused with an official renewal announcement.
